title: Western leaders announce SWIFT removal of Russian banks and central bank restrictions
body:
On 26 February 2022, two days after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the leaders of the United Kingdom, the European Commission, France, Germany, Italy, Canada and the United States issued a joint statement on further restrictive economic measures against Russia. The statement condemned the invasion and expressed support for the Ukrainian government and people.

The signatories committed to removing selected Russian banks from the SWIFT messaging system, which would cut them off from the international financial system and limit their global operations. They also committed to imposing restrictions on the Russian Central Bank to stop it from using its international reserves in ways that undermine the effect of the sanctions.

The statement announced further steps. The signatories pledged to limit the sale of citizenship, known as "golden passports", which allows wealthy Russians linked to the government to gain citizenship and access to Western financial systems. They also announced that a transatlantic task force would be launched the following week to enforce financial sanctions. The task force was to identify and freeze the assets of sanctioned individuals and companies in the signatories' jurisdictions, extending to officials, elites, their families and their enablers, and the signatories said they would work to disrupt the movement of illicit funds.
